text: P.F. Strawson's "Freedom and Resentment" (1962) argues that moral responsibility is grounded in...
choices: libertarian free will, which requires that determinism be false
our practices of reactive attitudes (resentment, gratitude, indignation), largely independent of whether determinism is true
the neuroscientific discovery of an uncaused decision center in the brain
a utilitarian calculation of the social benefits of praise and punishment
explanation: Strawson relocates responsibility from metaphysics to the reactive attitudes constitutive of interpersonal life, so the truth of determinism is largely beside the point. Option A is the incompatibilist libertarian view he sidesteps, C misrepresents his non-metaphysical approach, and D is a consequentialist theory of punishment, not Strawson's.
